title: Ride-On Paddy Field Ditching & Leveling Machine, Small Water Conservancy Tiller For Rice Farm
description:
Rice paddy field operation footage shows farmers operating a compact ride-on ditching and land leveling machine on muddy waterlogged farmland. The machine’s rotary mud wheel delivers stable traction in soft sludge without sinking, while the rear adjustable moldboard simultaneously levels field mud and digs uniform irrigation drainage ditches in one pass.
Traditional manual ditching relies on hoes, which is labor-intensive and produces uneven ditch depth. This integrated small agricultural machine combines land leveling and ditch forming functions, adapting to small scattered rice plots in mountain and hilly areas.
It can create consistent water channels for irrigation and drainage, optimize water distribution across rice paddies, greatly cutting farm labor time. The lightweight body makes flexible turning easy for narrow field ridges, widely used in early-stage rice field preparation before seedling transplanting.

title: Foam Sound Test 🔊
description:
Original Video Credit: IG/acousticpro_

Two different foam panels are placed in front of the same studio monitor to compare how they affect the sound. While both are commonly associated with audio treatment, the difference in what you hear is immediate.

The pyramid acoustic foam is designed to absorb sound reflections and reduce echo inside a room, not stop sound from passing through it. The rebonded foam is much denser, giving it far greater resistance to sound transmission and noticeably reducing the amount of noise that reaches the other side.

Understanding the difference between acoustic treatment and sound isolation is essential when building a studio, home theater, or recording space. Choosing the right material depends on whether you're trying to improve the sound within a room or prevent it from traveling beyond it.
